Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving fast with a 3-month pilot to validate inference quality and cost on a customer-facing feature (search summarization). A few quick asks so my execs can sign off: 

- Is it better to run the pilot on a metered hosted plan with temporary "burst credits" or to temporarily uplift us one tier for the pilot window?
- How do bundled features (KV cache, prefix caching, streaming) factor into pricing during a pilot?

Claire

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the context and the attachments. Short answer up front: for a short, tightly scoped 3-month pilot I usually recommend staying hosted + metered and adding a time-limited burst credit pool unless you need guaranteed throughput/SLA. Reasons: 

- Flexibility: no commit means you can iterate quick and avoid contract churn.
- Cost predictability: burst credits let you absorb higher-than-average token days without permanently changing pricing.
- Feature access: most packaging features (KV cache, streaming) are available on hosted plans; we can enable and configure them for the pilot.

However, if your pilot must demonstrate consistent p99 latency under steady load (attached slide suggests a 2k reqs/day steady period), a temporary tier uplift to our "Slate" tier (reserved throughput + higher SLA) reduces tail latency risk. That does carry a modest up-front commitment and a short-term prorated charge.

Ben/Lauren — can you run a two-line cost delta: (A) hosted metered + $X burst credits for 3 months vs (B) temporary uplift to Slate tier for 3 months with prorate and included feature bundle? I'll draft wording Claire can share with execs.

Vivek
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question for a 3-month pilot

Looping in numbers. Using Claire's monthly token estimate from orbis-usage-snapshot.csv:

- Baseline hosted metered (estimate): ~$3,200/month token spend + 20% safety buffer = ~$3,840/month.
- Burst credits option: one-time purchase of $6,000 burst pool that we burn down across 3 months (~$2,000/month effective).
- Combined hosted + burst: ~ $5,840/month effective for pilot (months 1–3).

- Temporary Slate uplift (prorated): Slate tier fixed fee $9,000/month (includes reserved throughput and TTL KV caching, lower p99). If we do a 3-month uplift and prorate start/stop: effective monthly = ~$9,000 (we can offer a pilot concession to $7,500/month to win this).

Tradeoffs: hosted+burst is ~35% cheaper and lower friction. Slate gives predictable latency and includes bundling (KV cache, priority routing, dedicated pool) that simplifies performance validation.

Notes on revert: standard uplift allows reversion at the end of the committed month with prorated billing; no penalty if we revert after the pilot window. If we include discounts or concessions (pilot discount), we document them in the MA/PO.

Ben
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Claire —

A few practical suggestions from an onboarding perspective: 

1) If you expect bursts tied to demos/marketing, go hosted + burst credits and we’ll enable auto-prefix caching and a small KV cache allocation. That reduces token spend and keeps operations light.
2) If you need to show deterministic p99 < 250ms to potential customers during the pilot, choose Slate uplift for the test weeks and we can schedule the uplift only during those heavy test windows.
3) We can include a one-time $1,500 onboarding services credit (prompt engineering + eval set run) if you commit to a signed pilot MA by 4/30.

If you want, I can produce two clear line items for the MA: (A) Hosted + Burst (monthly estimate, burst pool), (B) Slate uplift (monthly, concession). Which version would you prefer in the doc?

—Lauren
